caveats: A pipe is not a serial fd, the probe process is not the daemon, and the daemon has several threads where this has one. It is a proxy and may miss the real wait. It is still the wait of the same CLASS, and a proxy that fails to show a factor-of-eleven effect is worth reporting rather than discarding.
means: The probe does NOT separate the two load conditions. p99 wakeup latency is about 3 ms under load whether the load occupies all 8 cores or is pinned to 7, and p90 is unstable between repeats of the same condition - 1989 then 24 for all-8, 988 then 1002 for pinned. Meanwhile the daemon test fails 69% in one condition and 6% in the other.
oddity: Median latency is LOWER under load - about 9 us against 44 us idle - which is consistent with C-state exit latency at idle and is not what the hypothesis predicts either. Not investigated.
probe: two processes, reader blocked in select() on a pipe, writer busy-waiting to a 1 ms schedule, 2000 samples per condition. Two PROCESSES because a threaded version measures GIL handoff - the default switch interval is 5 ms - not kernel wakeup.
weakens: This bench's own reading of the free-core result as 'consistent with wakeup latency when every core is occupied'. Core availability changes the test outcome by a factor of eleven and does not change this probe's tail latency at all. As far as this probe reaches, wakeup latency does not explain it.
